This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 06.02.2020 passed in MVC.No.4659/2018 by the Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru City (for short 'the tribunal').

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation and erroneously fastening 20% contributory negligence as against the appellant- claimant.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 24.07.2018 at 1.20 p.m., the claimant was travelling on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-07- Y-1307 as a pillion rider, which was ridden by one N.Gangadhar along with another pillion rider namely, Pavan.
The motor cycle was being ridden by the said N.Gangadhar slowly and cautiously on the correct side of Hosakote-Chintamani Main Road at Sathyavara village.
At that time, one Eicher Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-01-AG-2290 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle to its rear side.

Due to the said impact,
the claimant fell down and sustained injuries.
He was immediately shifted to MVJ Medical College Hospital, Hosakote, wherein first aid treatment was given.
Thereafter, to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient for three days and he spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
In view of injuries suffered and financial expenditure expended, he filed a claim petition Sri R Kishore Kumar vs Abdul Mathin on 15 April, 2024

On service of notice, the respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their respective statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation and income of the claimant.
Respondent No.1 took up the plea that there were three people travelling on the motor cycle, which is illegal.
The rider of the motor cycle, who lost control over the vehicle was negligent for occurrence of the accident.
3.2 Respondent No.2-Insurance Company took up the plea that the accident occurred on 24.07.2018, but a complaint was lodged on 26.07.2018.
It was also pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence, whereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence,
Insurance Company would not be liable for the breach the terms and conditions of the policy.
Accordingly, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P16.

On the other hand, respondents examined two witnesses as RWs.1 and 2 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R5.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.2,97,000/- (future medical expenses does not carry any interest) with interest @ 7% per annum.
3.6 Being aggrieved by the inadequate compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation, NC: 2024:KHC:14955 which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
He further submits that the tribunal has erred in attributing the contributory negligence as against the appellant and the same may be set-aside.
On these grounds, he seeks to enhance the compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for appellant- claimant and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award, it is seen that the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P16, out of which, Exs.P1 to P3, P5 are the Police records, which clearly depict the filing of FIR and laying of charge sheet against the driver of the Sri R Kishore Kumar vs Abdul Mathin on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81480290/
3 offending vehicle and same has not been challenged or controverted.

sentences.text: Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence NC: 2024:KHC:14955 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Exs. P4,
P6 to P16 are the medical records, which clearly depict the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income, it is stated that age of the claimant was 18 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.

The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '18',
which does not call for interference.
The tribunal taken the income at Rs.8,000/- per month, in view of there being no proof of income.
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.12,500/- for the accident year 2018.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.12,500/-.
PW.2-Doctor has opined the disability to the extent of 38% to the lower limb and 13% to the whole body, whereas the tribunal has assessed the disability at 9% to the whole body.

Learned counsel for appellant- claimant contends that the disability assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side, whereas, learned counsel for Insurance Company objects the same and he sustains the NC: 2024:KHC:14955 judgment of the tribunal with regard to assessment of disability and so also the income taken by the tribunal.
8. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the disability requires to be taken at 11% to the whole body and the income requires to be taken at Rs.12,500/- per month.

Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.2,97,000/- (Rs.12,500/- x 12 x 18 x 11%) towards loss of future income due to disability as against Rs.1,55,500/- awarded by the tribunal.
9. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
10. The tribunal awarded Rs.2,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges.
However, the claimant was inpatient for 3 days.
Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.3,000/- under this head.
Towards medical expenses, Rs.1,14,500/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.24,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
In view of enhancement of the income by this Court to Rs.12,500/- per month, the claimant would require atleast three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled to Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 3) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
13. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.

Coming to the aspect of the liability and contributory negligence attributed against the rider of the motor cycle, it is seen that the tribunal has fixed the contributory negligence of 20% as against the rider of the motor cycle for triple riding.

It is apparently seen from the Police records that the FIR and charge sheet have been laid against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Eicher - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:14955 goods vehicle and no case has been filed against the rider of the motor cycle for triple riding and the same is also an offence under Sections 128 and 194C of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act').
17.

Learned counsel for appellant-claimant relied on the judgment in the case Mohammed Siddique and Another vs. National Insurance Company Limited and Others reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court Cases 520 at para No.13, which reads as under:
"But the above reason, in our view, is flawed.

sentences.text: The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.
Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two wheeled motor cycle, not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle.

Section 194C inserted by the Sri R Kishore Kumar vs Abdul Mathin on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81480290/
5 Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:14955 pillion riders.

sentences.text: Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.

It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree,
if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.

It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:14955 persons riding on a motor cycle.
It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motor cycle.
The fact that the motor cycle was hit by the car from behind, is admitted.
Interestingly, the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the deceased was wearing a helmet and that the deceased was knocked down after the car hit the motor cycle from behind, are all not assailed.

Therefore, the finding of the High Court that 2 persons on the pillion of the motor cycle, could have added to the imbalance, is nothing but presumptuous and is not based either upon pleading or upon the evidence on record.
Nothing was extracted from PW3 to the effect that 2 persons on the pillion added to the imbalance."
18. It is seen that in the present case, the claimant is one of the two pillion riders along with the rider of the motor cycle, who met with an accident and sustained injuries.

The tribunal has fastened 20%
contributory negligence against the rider of the motor cycle, strangely, the owner of the motor cycle was not made as a party to - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:14955 the claim petition, so also the Insurance Company of the motor cycle.

But,
factually there is no FIR or any offence made out against the rider of the motor cycle and the pillion riders by implicating them in any crime.

The FIR and charge sheet have been laid only against the Sri R Kishore Kumar vs Abdul Mathin on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81480290/
6 driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Eicher goods vehicle.

Admittedly, even according to the claimant,
the rider was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders and the Eicher goods vehicle/lorry came from behind and knocked them down, due to which the claimant suffered injuries.
The claimant herein is not the rider of the motor cycle, but he is one of the pillion riders.

The decision in the case of Mohammed Siddique and Another stated supra referred by the appellant is squarely applicable to this case on hand for setting aside the contributory negligence of 20% against the rider of the motor cycle as no where, it is pleaded that the accident occurred due to the negligence or contribution of the rider or the pillion riders of the motor cycle leading to the occurrence of accident.
Therefore, the saddling of 20% contributory negligence - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:14955 against the rider of the motor cycle cannot be sustained and the same is set aside.
The entire liability and negligence is fastened on the driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Eicher goods vehicle, which is insured with respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

19. Under the circumstances, this Court deems it appropriate to make certain observations with regard to pillion riders and riders, who ride the motor cycle with more than one pillion rider,
without wearing helmet, leading to occurrence of accident in the case of injury and also in case of death, which is the violation of Section 128 of the Act.

Section 128 reads as under:
"128. Safety measures for drivers and pillion riders.

- (1) No driver of a two-wheeled motor cycle shall carry more than one person in addition to himself on the motor cycle and no such person shall be carried otherwise than sitting on a proper seat securely fixed to the motor cycle behind the driver's seat with appropriate safety measures.

In addition to the safety measures mentioned in sub-section (1), the Central Government may, prescribe other safety measures for the drivers of two-wheeled motor cycles and pillion riders thereon."
20.

The penalty clause for violation of Section 128 of the Act is provided under Section 194C of the Act, which imposes a fine of one thousand rupees and the said person shall be disqualified for holding licence for a period of three months.

It is seen by this Court in several cases that where triple riding or riders and pillion riders not wearing helmet suffered injuries due to the accident are not brought to the books by implicating them in the crime by the Investigating Agency, so also the tribunal dealing in such cases does not fasten any liability with regard to offence committed by them and the penalty that should be imposed on them.

In such cases, even though the action is not taken or initiated by the Investigating Agency by not implicating the riders and pillion riders for triple riding or not wearing helmet and the same has been established - 17 - Sri R Kishore Kumar vs Abdul Mathin on 15 April, 2024

21. In the present case, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court Mohammed Siddique's case,
contributory negligence cannot be saddled against them for they did not contribute to the occurrence of the accident.
But, certainly they should be implicated for the provisions under Section 128 of the Act and penalty provisions under Section 194C of the Act.
